recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆大淋巴細胞，細胞質豐富呈淡藍色、邊緣略有稜角，一側含細小紫紅色嗜天青顆粒，核呈凹陷的不規則形；旁邊的嗜中性球可作大小對照，形態為大顆粒淋巴球，配合流式為 NK 細胞增多。
features: Large lymphocyte, larger than the adjacent neutrophil
Low to moderate N:C ratio with abundant pale blue cytoplasm and angular outline
Fine azurophilic granules clustered in the cytoplasm adjacent to the nuclear indentation
Indented, irregular nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin and no nucleoli
Adjacent normal segmented neutrophil; background red cells unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a large lymphocyte with abundant pale blue cytoplasm containing fine azurophilic granules and an indented nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin and no visible nucleoli. A normal segmented neutrophil lies adjacent for comparison. This is a large granular lymphocyte; morphology alone cannot determine NK versus T lineage. Findings are consistent with a large granular lymphocyte, supporting NK-cell lymphocytosis when flow cytometry shows surface CD3-negative, CD16/CD56-positive cells.

ddx.vs: T-LGL cells look identical but are surface CD3+/CD8+/CD57+ with clonal TCR rearrangement.
Reactive lymphocytes typically have deeply basophilic cytoplasm at the periphery that scallops around red cells and usually lack prominent azurophilic granules.
Aggressive NK-cell leukemia cells are more atypical, with immature chromatin and nucleoli, and are EBV-positive in a clinically fulminant setting.
Monocytes have gray-blue cytoplasm with fine dusty granules, vacuoles and folded lacy chromatin, rather than discrete azurophilic granules and condensed lymphoid chromatin.
